Aging and AMD associate with reduced enzymatic activities and altered balance (e.g., decreased SOD/CAT/GPx activities systemically and in ocular tissues; compensatory transcriptional upregulation with functional decline in activity), linking enzyme capacity to disease state (colak2019antioxidantsandagerelated pages 15-18, hsueh2022thepathomechanismantioxidant pages 10-12, colak2019antioxidantsandagerelated pages 13-15). Genetic and interventional models causally implicate these enzymes: Sod1 deficiency produces AMD-like retinal pathology, GPx4 overexpression protects retina, and catalase delivery to RPE is cytoprotective (colak2019antioxidantsandagerelated pages 20-22). Clinically, lower GR/GPx activities and reduced total antioxidant status associate with AMD presence and severity, supporting translational relevance (colak2019antioxidantsandagerelated pages 13-15, colak2019antioxidantsandagerelated pages 5-8, ulanczyk2020dietaryandlifestyle pages 11-13).

Previous Use: Enzymatic antioxidant activity assays are established PD and mechanistic endpoints in RPE drug discovery and validation: compounds enhancing antioxidant enzyme expression/activity protect ARPE-19 from oxidant-induced death, miRNA modulation of CAT alters stress responses, and SOD/CAT enzyme conjugates and gene therapies showed efficacy in preclinical testing (colak2019antioxidantsandagerelated pages 15-18, colak2019antioxidantsandagerelated pages 20-22).
